name: Paper Tower

scoring.report_note: Report team-level deltas only. Never rank teams or individuals — the tower measures the team's working habits, not talent.

description: Two-minute pre/post measure for the Paper Tower team challenge. Scores at team level: how did shared planning, role clarity, information flow and recovery from failure change across the build?

instructions.pre: Before teams form. Each participant answers alone, about their own last week at work — not about the exercise.
instructions.post: Immediately after the debrief. Same items, now answered about the build just completed, as a team.

items.pre_text: Before my team starts building, we sketch the plan together.
items.post_text: During the build, we sketched or named the plan together before touching tape.

items.pre_text: On my team, I know which part is mine without being told.
items.post_text: During the build, everyone knew which part was theirs.

items.pre_text: I keep useful observations to myself when the room is busy.
items.post_text: During the build, useful observations stayed unspoken while hands were busy.

items.pre_text: When something we built fails, we pause and change one thing.
items.post_text: When the tower leaned or fell, we paused and changed one thing.

items.pre_text: The loudest voice on my team usually sets the direction.
items.post_text: During the build, the loudest voice set the direction while others just held tape.

items.pre_text: I can name the trade my team is making between speed and stability.
items.post_text: The book test made us name the speed-versus-stability trade we had made.

report.title: Paper Tower — team collaboration delta
sections: Judge-card scores: height, book test, self-rated arguments
One suggested working-habit change per team, derived from the largest positive delta
